issues.title: Brownian-bridge control is outside the stated admissible class

failure_location.quote:
Then we may take the feedback control $\bar\theta_t=\frac{\xi-X^{0,x_0;\bar\theta}_t}{1-t} \textbf{1}_{[0,1)}(t)$ and the Brownian bridge theory 
(see \cite{karatzas1998brownian}) implies that $X_1^{0,x_0;\theta}=\xi$ almost surely (a.s. for short).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the set of admissible controls, denoted by $\Theta$, consists of all such control processes on $[0,1]$ that are square-integrable on $\Omega\times [0,1]$

issues.failure_explanation: For the displayed Brownian bridge, the drift equals xi-x_0 minus the stochastic integral of (1-s)^{-1}. Consequently its second moment contains d t/(1-t), whose integral over [0,1] diverges. Thus the paper cannot 'take' this control from the old class of controls square-integrable on Omega times [0,1], and the asserted exact equivalence does not follow from that construction. By contrast, the L2 norm of its time integral of absolute value is finite because the singularity is only of order (1-t)^{-1/2} after taking the pointwise L2 norm.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory exact-equivalence claim has an invalid admissibility step. The later truncated Brownian-bridge convergence construction and finite-cost regularized controls are not defeated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use, for the unregularized problem, an admissible class of adapted controls satisfying E[(∫₀¹|θ_s|ds)²]<∞, and verify by the Brownian-bridge moment estimate and Minkowski's inequality that the displayed bridge control belongs to it. The regularized problem may retain the finite-energy effective domain, with controls having infinite ∫₀¹|θ_s|²ds assigned infinite cost.
issues.why_classification: The old equivalence argument genuinely uses a control excluded by its stated class, so this is not a typo. A short, routine integrability correction restores exact endpoint pinning and the equivalence while leaving the finite-cost regularized controls, later convergence construction, and rates unchanged.

issues.title: Headline value bound omits expectation over random initial data
issues.failure_explanation: The old headline claims a pointwise bound for the random quantity V_epsilon(0,x_0), whereas the detailed Brownian-bridge and verification arguments establish a bound after expectation. For example, an unbounded square-integrable random x_0 and the admissible objective G(x)=|x| make V_epsilon(0,x_0) an unbounded random variable, so it cannot satisfy an almost-sure bound by a deterministic constant depending only on moments. The expected quantity is nevertheless controlled at the stated order.
issues.overall_effect: Only the finite-dimensional summary theorem overstates the detailed convergence results; those expected-value results and their rate remain intact.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the headline estimate as |E[V_ε(0,x₀)]−G(ξ)|≤Cε log(1/ε), equivalently with the established nonnegative one-sided difference, while retaining the same assumptions, rate, and constant dependence. Do not assert an almost-sure bound for V_ε(0,x₀).
issues.why_classification: The detailed results directly supply the expected-value estimate, so no new proof architecture is needed. Nevertheless, replacing a pointwise bound for a random quantity by an expectation is a meaningful weakening of probability mode, as unbounded square-integrable initial data disprove the former; the surviving estimate remains recognizably comparable, making the issue moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.title: Mean-field verification square is missing the epsilon scaling
issues.failure_explanation: Writing p for the Lions derivative, the relevant terms satisfy epsilon|theta|^2/2 + theta·p + |p|^2/(2epsilon) = |epsilon theta+p|^2/(2epsilon). The old square |theta+p|^2/(2epsilon) has the wrong theta-squared and cross-term coefficients and therefore gives the wrong minimizer theta=-p rather than theta=-p/epsilon. This invalidates the displayed fundamental identity used by the verification proof.
issues.overall_effect: The verification proof of identification and uniqueness fails as written, and the proposition's uniqueness conclusion, which invokes this lemma, loses that support. The correctly scaled FBSDE elsewhere is consistent with the repaired formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Writing p for the Lions derivative, replace the verification remainder by |εθ_s+p|²/(2ε) and replace the asserted minimizing feedback by θ_s*=−p/ε. Apply this corrected completion of squares in the lemma and in the proposition's invocation of the lemma.
issues.why_classification: The old proof uses the incorrectly scaled square to identify the wrong minimizer, so the defect is substantive rather than purely transcriptional. The correction is nevertheless a local, routine algebraic repair, is uniquely consistent with the cost, master equation, and FBSDE, and restores the same identification and uniqueness conclusions throughout the affected chain.

issues.title: Pointwise Lions-derivative bounds do not follow from the averaged tangent estimate

failure_location.quote: applying It\^o's formulas, we obtain $|\delta X_1|\leq |\phi(\xi)|$ a.s.

issues.failure_explanation: The Itô calculation based on the total Hessian gives nonnegativity of an expected inner product and hence at most an L2 contraction for the tangent state. It does not imply the samplewise inequality claimed in the proof. Moreover, the resulting directional L2-to-L1 estimate does not isolate the two separate pointwise kernels partial-x partial-mu V and partial-mu-mu V. The latest proof instead establishes an L1 contraction through a normalized supermartingale and uses a distinct coercive directional system to obtain the kernel bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition's epsilon-uniform pointwise second-order Lions-derivative estimates are unproved, so the uniform-in-epsilon clause of the particle approximation theorem is unsupported. The base O(1/N) estimate under Assumption ass:smoothness is not directly defeated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State a regular coercive hypothesis set sufficient for pointwise kernel control, including the needed higher regularity, averaged convexity, and a bound ∂x∂μG≥κI. Replace the invalid samplewise-contraction step by the normalized-supermartingale L1 contraction and use the separate coercive spatial and measure-directional systems to derive the pointwise or μ-almost-everywhere kernel bounds. Condition the ε-uniform clause of the particle theorem on these corrected hypotheses.
issues.why_classification: An averaged L2 tangent estimate cannot be converted into the claimed pointwise Lions-kernel bounds by a local calculation. The established repair requires a substantial but contained replacement argument and a limited restriction to a regular coercive class. It preserves recognizable ε-uniform derivative estimates and the dependent O(1/N) guarantee without reconstructing the rest of the particle approximation theory, so moderate is the least adequate class.

issues.title: Mean-field algorithm does not implement the joint-cloud estimator
issues.failure_explanation: In the old source G is a functional on probability measures, so G(Y_{i,j};tilde-mu_T) has no defined general-functional interface. More importantly, the exact formula at beta uses, for each Monte Carlo index, one jointly sampled N-particle terminal configuration: its common exponential weight and Y_{i,j} must come from that same configuration. The frozen background and independently particle-indexed weights in the old pseudocode do not implement this expectation.
issues.overall_effect: The general mean-field Monte Carlo procedure is undefined and does not simulate the represented optimal-control estimator. The analytical value-function and particle-convergence results do not depend on this pseudocode.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each Monte Carlo index j, jointly sample all N terminal candidates Y_{1,j},…,Y_{N,j}, form μ_T^(j)=N⁻¹∑ᵣδ_{Y_{r,j}}, and compute the single common weight w_j=exp(−NG(μ_T^(j))/ε). Then use β_i=∑ⱼw_jY_{i,j}/∑ⱼw_j for every particle i, eliminating the undefined particlewise call G(Y_{i,j};μ̃_T).
issues.why_classification: The old pseudocode is genuinely undefined for a general functional and has the wrong sampling dependence, so it is not a typo. The exact joint-cloud estimator is already displayed in the old source, however, and translating it into the corrected sampling loop is a short, routine, source-supported algorithmic repair with no change to the analytical results or intended output.
